heading: Defense Technology Intelligence
subheading: AI battlefield software, drones, autonomy & European rearmament
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Defense names carry policy, program-concentration, and valuation risk. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: European Allies and Canada raised 2025 defence spending nearly 20% YoY, with several already tracking the Hague summit's 3.5%-of-GDP core guideline years ahead of the 2035 deadline, while the EU's €800B 'ReArm Europe' framework keeps the multi-year runway intact

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD · DEFENSE TECH VC, PAST 2025's $9.6B FULL-YEAR RECORD
kpis.label: Early-stage defense-tech rounds are pricing at 17x-50x revenue, and the BIS keeps comparing the sector's scarcity-driven valuations to the AI-infrastructure buildout it already calls bubble-like; Anduril's targeted raise (last discussed near $100B) remains unclosed roughly ten weeks after first being reported on Jul 24

Defense Autonomous Warfare Group request inside a record $75B FY27 drone/counter-drone budget ask; separately, 98% of Golden Dome's requested $17.5-17.9B needs a reconciliation bill rather than the base budget, so a continuing resolution would leave the program with no funding at all rather than merely freezing it

kpis.sub: ANDURIL'S AIR FORCE CCA PRODUCTION AWARD · SEP 26
kpis.label: The Air Force named Anduril's FQ-44A 'Fury' (alongside General Atomics' FQ-42A 'Vengeance') for Collaborative Combat Aircraft production — 150 airframes initially, scaling toward 500 by 2032 at roughly $20M/unit, split between the two primes — plus a separate autonomy-software contract for Anduril; a real production milestone that strengthens the case for an eventual IPO even as its private funding round drags on

tiers.label: Established / Software & Primes
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Shares near $183 (Sep 22-23) sit between a ~$214 bull case (93% revenue growth, sovereign-AI demand, 26 upward FY2027 EPS revisions in 30 days with zero cuts) and a ~$159 bear case built on a 79x forward P/E versus ServiceNow's 27x; consensus targets cluster near $186, effectively a Hold
rows.watch for: CEO Alex Karp's Sep 17 comment that leading AI labs may need to be nationalized adds a regulatory-risk thread, and the valuation leaves almost no room for growth to decelerate below the ~60%+ pace analysts are pricing in

rows.angle: Order backlog reached €80.5B at the end of June, but shares have slipped back to roughly €993 — down ~36% YTD and about half their €2,007 52-week high — as investor focus shifts from celebrating new orders to scrutinizing execution
rows.watch for: Delivery delays on wheeled armored vehicles and Skyranger air-defense systems, suspected quality issues with protective plates, negative operating free cash flow from postponed advance payments/inventory build, and July's loss of the €12.8B F126 frigate program all sit under CEO Armin Papperger's leadership

rows.angle: New CEO Sam Mehta and new board chair Lewis Hay are settling in after Chris Kubasik's conduct-related ouster; the $4.7B Lockheed Martin deal and continued VAMPIRE/APKWS combat use in Ukraine keep the underlying business humming
rows.watch for: The Kubasik departure still hasn't been explained, and Golden Dome's FY27 funding — 98% of which needs a reconciliation bill — is now understood to be at real risk under any stopgap

rows.angle: Shares are holding this month's recovery near the mid-2,000s pence range on the record £84.0B H1 order backlog and July's raised full-year guidance (8-10% sales growth, 11-13% EPS growth), with no fresh negative catalyst this week
rows.watch for: Shares remain below the 2,360p 52-week high, and H2 execution against the raised guidance is still unproven — the market has stopped rewarding new order announcements on their own

tiers.label: High-Growth Autonomy Pure-Plays
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Despite the Sep 2-3 $464.8M Army LOCUST X3 laser award — the Pentagon's first-ever directed-energy production contract — shares trade around $147, down roughly 40% over the past year and 25% in the last month alone
rows.watch for: A prior-year $265.1M GAAP net loss, a $240.7M goodwill impairment, and a $1.49B unfunded-backlog write-off from the BADGER/SCAR cancellation still weigh on sentiment; consensus FY28 EPS was cut from $5.38 to $4.39 in 90 days (9 cuts in the last 30 days) and CEO Wahid Nawabi sold ~$3.9M of stock on Jun 29 — the $225.77 average target implies large upside only if execution actually shows up

rows.angle: Sell-side targets kept climbing after the Q2 beat-and-raise (Canaccord $135, consensus ~$105.62, Strong Buy), and GE Aerospace's GEK800 engine testing keeps CCA-engine optionality alive toward a targeted $150M of 2027 turbojet revenue — a thesis that gained credibility when Sep 26 confirmed the CCA program is now moving into real production dollars
rows.watch for: Kratos qualified for both rounds of the Pentagon's Drone Dominance Program but again failed to make the Sep 18 Gauntlet II leaderboard — a real data point against the near-term autonomy-optionality case

rows.angle: Teal Drones missed the top five in Gauntlet II's Close Quarters Battle category (Sep 18-19); shares have mostly moved with broad high-beta drone-sector sentiment through September — down on risk-off days, up on risk-on ones — rather than on company-specific news
rows.watch for: The Blue Ops/Havoc maritime-autonomy story and the Apium Swarm Robotics integration still need to convert into contracted revenue rather than platform narrative, on top of August's insider share sales

rows.angle: Ascent Aerosystems missed the top five in Gauntlet II's Deep Strike category (Sep 18); the core Sentrycs/Iron Drone counter-UAS business and an Army loitering-munitions program continue in the background while shares swing 4-6% with sector-wide risk sentiment
rows.watch for: The Q2 EPS miss (-$0.19 vs -$0.13 expected) and a Form 144 insider-sale filing remain live balance-sheet concerns on top of the Gauntlet II result

private_watchlist.name: Anduril
private_watchlist.note: The funding talks first reported Jul 24 remain unclosed roughly ten weeks later. Far more concretely, the Air Force named Anduril's FQ-44A Fury for CCA production on Sep 26 — up to ~$5B of hardware revenue split with General Atomics, plus a separate autonomy-software award — real production dollars that strengthen the eventual-IPO case regardless of when (or at what mark) the private round closes.

private_watchlist.name: Shield AI
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the ~$1.5-2B round (Mar 2026). Continuing to compete for the Navy's up-to-$800M ISR task-order pool with the V-BAT drone, alongside a run of NATO eastern-flank orders (Greece, Poland).

private_watchlist.name: Saronic
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the $1.75B Series D plus an early-September add-on. Continuing to build out its Port of Gulfport test site toward a stated target of 20+ autonomous surface vessels a year by 2027.

private_watchlist.name: Helsing
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the $1.8B Series E closed Jul 13 — the largest defence-tech round in European history. Continues fielding the HX-2 strike drone in Ukraine and building out its Altra battle-management software.

bear_case.title: Public-market valuations remain stretched
bear_case.description: Palantir at ~$183 still trades around a 79x forward P/E versus ServiceNow's 27x, and the S&P Aerospace & Defense sub-index sits near 32x forward earnings versus roughly 20x for the broader S&P 500 — a premium the sector has to keep earning, not just borrowing against sentiment.

bear_case.title: Private-market valuations are drawing bubble comparisons of their own
bear_case.description: Early-stage defense-tech rounds are pricing at 17x-50x revenue, and Anduril's targeted ~$100B valuation remains unclosed roughly ten weeks after first being reported; the Bank for International Settlements has begun comparing the sector's forward-looking pricing to the AI-infrastructure buildout it already calls bubble-like.

bear_case.title: The Pentagon's own drone competitions keep favoring private newcomers over listed pure-plays
bear_case.description: Sep 18's Gauntlet II results put Neros, Perennial Autonomy, ORQA, XTEND and ModalAI atop the leaderboard, while Red Cat's Teal Drones, Ondas's Ascent Aerosystems and Kratos — all three publicly listed — missed the top five in their categories again.

bear_case.title: Contract wins aren't rescuing the pure-play stocks that win them
bear_case.description: AeroVironment's $464.8M Army laser award hasn't stopped shares from falling ~40% over the past year and 25% in the last month, alongside nine downward EPS revisions in 30 days and a CEO share sale — a reminder that a good contract doesn't retroactively fix a damaged balance sheet or reset analyst confidence.
bear_case.counter: The $225.77 average analyst target still implies substantial upside if the laser and backlog growth actually convert to earnings.

bear_case.title: Golden Dome's funding structure means a stopgap doesn't freeze it — it zeroes it
bear_case.description: 98% of Golden Dome's requested $17.5-17.9B FY27 funding needs a reconciliation bill, not the base defense budget; a continuing resolution locks agencies at prior-year spending, which for Golden Dome is nothing, since the program has no FY26 baseline to revert to.

bear_case.title: Rheinmetall's backlog no longer moves the stock — execution does
bear_case.description: A record €80.5B order backlog didn't stop shares from sliding back to ~€993; delivery delays, suspected quality issues, negative operating free cash flow and July's €12.8B F126 loss show that order announcements alone no longer drive the share price the way they did earlier in the rearmament cycle.

catalysts.description: Up to ~$5B split with General Atomics across 150 initial airframes (scaling to 500 by 2032), plus a separate autonomy-software award — a real production milestone for the collaborative-combat-aircraft program.

catalysts.description: Neros, Perennial Autonomy, ORQA, XTEND and ModalAI top the categories; Red Cat's Teal Drones, Ondas's Ascent Aerosystems and Kratos all miss the top five again.

catalysts.title: Rheinmetall's backlog hits €80.5B but the stock keeps sliding
catalysts.description: Investors shift from rewarding new orders to demanding delivery, amid Skyranger delays, quality concerns and July's €12.8B F126 frigate-program loss.

catalysts.description: The Pentagon's first directed-energy production contract briefly lifted shares, but nine EPS downgrades in 30 days and a CEO share sale kept the stock down ~25% for the month.

catalysts.description: First reported Jul 24, still not confirmed closed roughly ten weeks later, even as the company lands real production contracts.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: BAE Systems
positions.note: The record £84.0B H1 backlog and raised full-year guidance are unchanged and shares are holding this month's recovery with no fresh negative catalyst — still the least-disputed thesis on this page. Directly accessible from the UK with no wrapper needed.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Sell-side targets keep climbing on GEK800 CCA-engine testing, and Sep 26's Anduril CCA production award confirms the whole collaborative-combat-aircraft ecosystem — engines included — is moving from R&D into production dollars; weight raised, though Kratos still hasn't placed on a Gauntlet leaderboard. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: The $464.8M laser contract is real diversification, but shares are down ~40% over the past year and 25% in the last month, with nine EPS downgrades in 30 days and a CEO share sale on top of a prior-year $265.1M net loss — weight trimmed to reflect how much execution still has to happen before the $225.77 average target means anything. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: A new CEO and chair are in place and real contracts keep landing ($4.7B Lockheed deal, VAMPIRE/APKWS in Ukraine), but the Kubasik ouster is still unexplained and Golden Dome's FY27 funding is understood to be zero, not frozen, under a stopgap — unresolved, not a buy signal yet. Also sits in the Space sleeve via satellite work — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Rheinmetall
positions.note: A €80.5B backlog didn't stop shares sliding back to ~€993; delivery delays, quality concerns, negative free cash flow and July's €12.8B F126 loss are concrete new execution evidence this week, not just sentiment — stays a watch, and conviction moved lower even though the category didn't change. Directly accessible from the UK without a wrapper.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Shares near $183 sit exactly between a ~$214 bull case and a ~$159 bear case built on a 79x forward P/E versus ServiceNow's 27x — a genuine growth story (26 EPS raises in 30 days, zero cuts) priced for perfection, plus Karp's nationalization comments as a fresh regulatory-risk thread. Also anchors the AI sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Ondas Holdings
positions.note: Ascent Aerosystems missed Gauntlet II's Deep Strike top five again, and shares are swinging 4-6% on broad sector sentiment rather than company news — nothing here contradicts Avoid.

positions.name: Red Cat Holdings
positions.note: Teal Drones again missed the Gauntlet II podium, and the stock keeps trading on broad drone-sector risk sentiment rather than its own news — still nothing to justify moving off Avoid.
